title: Thomas Sankara's birth chart
metaDescription: Thomas Sankara's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 29.3° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled fall in cardinal signs, the widest weighting the unknown hour leaves certain. The cardinal signs begin things; a chart weighted there treats every stall as a starting gun.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 29.3° into Sagittarius — the third decan, which the old scheme hands to the Sun. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 15.3° Capricorn, Venus holds 11.7° Aquarius, Mars holds 28.1° Virgo — in the old shorthand, thought with its feet on the ground; attraction that begins as conversation; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Neptune and Pluto — a sextile holding at 0.8°. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, the Sun square Mars at 1.2°, and Mercury square Neptune at 1.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Uranus while both square Mars. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags a single placement in this chart. The Moon in Capricorn at 21.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: earth 4, air 3, fire 2, water 1 across the elements, and cardinal 4, mutable 3, fixed 3 across the modalities. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.8° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 21.8°.
